title: Design docs and UML
idea: Design documentation is a short written record of scope, key decisions and diagrams, so a reader understands the system without reading the code.
points: A class diagram shows structure: classes, interfaces and how they connect.
A sequence diagram shows behaviour: who calls whom, in order, for one use case.
A one-page design doc states scope, decisions with reasons, and links to diagrams.
Keep diagrams as text files next to the code, so reviews diff them.

code.title: One-page design doc
code.caption: Scope, each decision with its reason and the option it rejected, and links to the diagrams.

pitfalls: Do not draw every getter and field; show only types and calls that explain the design.
A decision without its reason invites the same debate again; write the why.
Update the diagram in the same change as the code, or it silently goes stale.

quiz.q: A reviewer asks when listeners hear about a booking. Which artefact answers best?
options: The scope section of the design doc
quiz.why: Timing is behaviour. The sequence diagram orders the calls: `onBooked` comes only after `save`. A class diagram shows links, not order.

takeaway: Class diagrams show structure, sequence diagrams show order, docs explain why.
